chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Head arrangements, Herschel Evans' ear and Lester Young's reading
summary: Moten could not head, but with Basie riffs Durham wrote leads and Herschel Evans harmonized by ear; Lester read well but needed time.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But, I mean, mostly -- a lot of the stuff they played, was it heads or --
No, they didn't do too much heading. Ed Lewis and I were talking about that the other day. No, they wouldn't have been able to do any heads. Now, a lot of

heads came in when we got with Basie. Because I could write out a background of riff, what we call it, for the sax player background? Just write the lead? Herschel and those guys would play their harmony right with it, didn't have to write it. Say, write it later, when you get ready to publish. So that's how Charlie Hathaway came in, and got credit, and Buck Linn, Ram because they had to score the harmony. And there were a lot of things I made my harmony on, too, backgrounds and a lot of things. Can make a lot of skeletons. But they didn't do much heading then. Lewis and myself was talking about that the other day. Benny Morton couldn't head.
Well, I think --
He couldn't do much heading.
No, I think it was -- let's see, it was Dickie Wells who told me that Herschel (inaudible) got so difficult about it, because Herschel used to like to lose his power or something.
Yeah, well, Herschel wasn't a good reader.
No.
But he was a good ear man. Because you can write four-part harmony, sax, and pass it out, invent it the first time, and he'd play down what you're supposed to have for him.
(Inaudible) got it.
Yeah, that other fourth part.
Yeah.
Every time, or just about. Lester was pretty good at that, too. But Herschel was the king.
Who was?
Herschel.
Yeah.
Lester was pretty good at that , too.
Oh, was he? That was -- he could read.
He could read pretty good. Nobody could read what I could write, all the way down the line.
He was lazy, though.
Yeah, we'd have to interpret it to him, give him time to get it.
